content:
Apple is preparing for a more focused, and potentially more expensive, iPhone launch this fall.

First, the cheaper entry-level iPhone 18 will be held back until spring next year, meaning the September slot will be carried by higher-priced Pro models, as well as Apple's first foldable iPhone Ultra, with a starting price expected to be higher than usual.

Below is how new and upgrading customers can digest this "shock pricing" in advance.

Apple Upgrade lowers monthly payments

First, Apple launched a new program called "Apple Upgrade" in partnership with Klarna in July. Customers can choose to lease an iPhone for 12 or 24 months. Because monthly payments cover only part of the device price, the monthly fee is lower than traditional instalment plans.

When the lease ends, customers can choose to upgrade, return the iPhone, or pay off the balance to own the device. AppleCare must be purchased separately, but AppleCare One can bundle multiple coverages together at a more favourable price.

Apple Upgrade allows the company to display a more digestible monthly figure alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra. This is key, since rumours suggest one of these phones could be priced as high as US$2,500, approaching MacBook Pro territory.

Apple raises iPhone trade-in values

Next, Apple today (local time) raised the trade-in values for most of its products.

The maximum trade-in value for the iPhone 16 Pro Max has been raised from US$695 to US$720. The iPhone 16 Pro has seen an even larger increase, from US$560 to US$630.

Customers can apply the credit toward a traditional purchase or the Apple Upgrade leasing plan. With higher trade-in values, lease monthly payments can be reduced further.

After the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra officially launch in September, Apple should also accept current iPhone models for trade-in at that point.

Apple expands Android trade-in eligibility

Finally, Apple is actively courting Android users. The updated trade-in list has added more Google, Samsung, and OnePlus models, including the Pixel 9 series, Galaxy S21 Ultra, OnePlus 13, and OnePlus 13R.

These users can likewise apply the credit toward a purchase or the Apple Upgrade leasing plan. In other words, Apple is widening the entry point to its ecosystem just as new phone prices climb further.

These moves do not make the iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone Ultra cheap, but they reduce the visible monthly outlay, lift the value of older devices, and offer a path over for more Android users.

Overall, these changes help Apple sell what is set to be its most expensive lineup of iPhones to date. Customers who want to upgrade but avoid the steep pricing should keep an eye on the standard iPhone 18 and the cheaper iPhone 18e, expected around March or April next year.
